translationRepairs: The Supreme Ancestor often passed through Xianyang, gazed upon the Qin emperor, sighed deeply, said: "Alas, a great man should be like this!"
The Supreme Ancestor often performed corvée service at Xianyang and was allowed to observe the Qin emperor; he sighed deeply and said: "Alas, a great man should be like this!"
繇咸陽 is corvée duty at Xianyang and 縱觀 is being allowed to observe, so the original 'passed through'/'gazed' is wrong; but 常 means 'often', not 'once', so the proposal must keep that sense.
He made him read the faces of the two children, saw Emperor Xiaohui, said: "Madame's nobility comes from this male child."
She had him read the faces of the two children; when he saw Emperor Xiaohui, he said: "Madame's nobility comes from this male child."

Preceding units make Empress Lü the agent who fed the old man; 令相兩子 is her having him physiognomize the two children, so the original ambiguous 'He made him' is wrong and the proposed subject is right.

The old man had already left; Gaozu had just come from the neighboring house. Empress Lü told him in full that a guest had passed by and read the faces of her and the children and mother—all were greatly noble.
The old man had already left; Gaozu had just come from the neighboring house. Empress Lü told him in full that a guest had passed by and read the faces of her and her children—all were greatly noble.
相我子母 means physiognomizing mother-and-children as one unit (Empress Lü and her children); the original invents a separate 'mother' beyond Empress Lü.
The old father said: 'Just now madam and children all take after you, your features noble beyond words.'
The old father said: 'Just now, madam and the children were all judged noble because of you; your features show nobility beyond words.'
皆以君 is causal ('because of you'), not resemblance ('take after you'); the proposal correctly ties their judged nobility to Gaozu and keeps 君相貴不可言.
